hypothesis.statement: The residual scratch band is a one-register rotation, and every register named here is quoted at its DEFINING instruction with its stream offset. OURS: row is defined at `@0x178 li r8,0` and updated at `@0x1d4 addi r8,r8,1`; srcOffset at `@0x17c li r3,0` and `@0x1ec addi r3,r3,4`; dstOffset at `@0x184 li r9,0` and `@0x1e4 addi r9,r9,16`. TARGET: row at `@0x178 li r9,0` and `@0x1d4 addi r9,r9,1`; dstOffset at `@0x17c li r3,0` and `@0x1ec addi r3,r3,16`; srcOffset at `@0x184 li r4,0` and `@0x1e4 addi r4,r4,4`. So the target numbers dstOffset BELOW srcOffset and puts row at the top of the band, while ours numbers srcOffset lowest and row below dstOffset. Because dstOffset is the only scratch whose live range spans the whole outer loop AND is initialised outside it, the untried lever is to give the do-loop a second outer-scope integer that is live across the loop (so the allocator has to rank dstOffset against a peer) rather than reordering the two it already has - every reordering form is now proven not to reach codegen.
